authoring: Hand-authored for the decisive chains of the iteration-6 cycles only. Validated at build time by repurposing_view.py: every card id, need id and PMID must exist, every edge carries a type and a source id, every chain has the six columns and is connected from an observation to an experiment. No central knowledge graph and no data store: this file is the whole graph. Card F04 (P9) was not on main when this file was written; the excitatory-gain chain uses F01 and the P11 magnesium card, and F04 nodes are added here after that merge (a regeneration then picks them up).

chains.title: Glial reactivity
chains.question: Is glial activation in a Wwox-deficient brain a readout, a seizure consequence or a lever, given that its sign differs between systems?

nodes.label: Null and P47T mouse: more GFAP and IBA1 signal (excess)
Mutant rat cortex: about half the GFAP+ and Iba1+ cells of wild type from PND 5 (deficit)
Human WWOX-knockout organoid: no reactive programme, microglia absent
Need: neuroinflammation and gliosis; the sign of the glial difference is not settled
UNRESOLVED: species, allele, region, assay and age window are confounded
Gliosis may be partly secondary to neuronal dysfunction or seizures
J01 glial-reactivity modulators: abstention, no premise for the direction of a lever
Neuron-restricted AAV9 lowers GFAP+ cells (about 44 to about 5): an indirect effect, not glial modulation
Same-animal time course P5 to P17: glial density with continuous recording, each animal classed before or after its first spike

edges.note: Also P47T mouse (PMID 36828035).
Opposite sign; the authors state the contrast.
Neuron-restricted rescue also normalises seizures and survival, so the lowering is indirect.
No premise for a lever: the card abstains.
No glial endpoint after any compound in a Wwox-deficient system has been measured.
Separates a seizure consequence from a seizure-independent signal.

chains.title: NMDAR gate and magnesium
chains.question: Does the bursting of Wwox-deficient slices reflect a NMDAR gain, and can a graded rise in extracellular magnesium reach it?

nodes.label: Neuron-specific knockout slices burst: 36 of 42 knockout, 4 of 23 heterozygote, 0 of 11 wild type
The competitive NMDAR antagonist d-APV abolishes the bursting (5 slices from 3 animals)
Knockout neurons rest more depolarised (-73.6 against -79.3 mV); inhibitory current amplitude about halved
Need: excitatory gain at the d-APV-sensitive glutamate-receptor node
Mg2+ blocks the NMDAR pore in a voltage-dependent way, so a depolarised cell has a weaker block (arithmetic only, other cell type)
Bursting occurs in a medium with Mg2+; whether the NMDAR dependence is permissive or a gain is untested
F01 glutamate-receptor node: d-APV is a tool compound; graded block by a clinical antagonist untested in WWOX
P11 extracellular magnesium as the NMDAR gate (class level, nutrient route)
GRIN-variant series (not WWOX): memantine benefit in 14 of 19 gain-of-function against 3 of 15 other variants
Healthy mice: oral magnesium sulfate raised serum but not cerebrospinal-fluid Mg; the threonate did
Infants with West syndrome: oral magnesium arm with ACTH, no difference in seizure control (48 analysed)
Graded bath Mg2+ in knockout, heterozygote and wild-type slices in the source medium, d-APV as ceiling; serum and CSF Mg in the mouse
Graded memantine against perampanel against d-APV in Wwox-deficient slices with wild-type, heterozygote and vehicle arms

edges.note: One drug, one preparation; a full block is not a partial block.
Both measurements predict a weaker block at rest; no NMDAR current or magnesium sensitivity was measured in a WWOX system.
Retrospective series in another disease; the sign depends on the variant class.
Healthy mice; exposure, not efficacy.
Different aetiology and regimen; shows no efficacy signal for the oral arm.

chains.title: Missense protein and route blockade
chains.question: If a destabilised missense protein is cleared, does blocking the route return protein that carries function, and by which route is it cleared?

nodes.label: Fibroblasts homozygous for the Q230P missense: transcript comparable to controls, no WWOX band on one membrane
A different SDR missense (P252A) in thyroid-cancer lines: low protein, normal mRNA, faster turnover, lysosomal route
Need: rescue a destabilised SDR-domain missense protein
Premise: the protein is made and then cleared; synthesis, solubility and degradation are not separated for Q230P
The route may be lysosomal, not proteasomal, for this lesion class (read from P252A)
A02 proteasome-inhibitor class: route blockade, hypothesis at class level
Cystathionine beta-synthase alleles: blockade sufficed for S466L, helped three catalytic-domain alleles, failed for T191M
Same enzyme: wild type rises too; effective exposure damaged cells; tolerated exposure gave no significant activity gain
ASPA C152W: blocking the route accumulated insoluble, inert protein (activity not measurable)
Isogenic null neural line: route arms, solubility and native fractions, half-life, transgene mRNA, function ruler; outcomes fixed in advance

edges.note: Another allele: no read-across between missense alleles.

chains.title: Rescue window of gene addition
chains.question: Is the benefit of WWOX re-expression a prevention inside the first days of life, or also a recovery after the phenotype has appeared?

nodes.label: Null mouse: hypoglycaemia from the second week, survival of about three weeks
Neuron-specific deletion reproduces the phenotype; oligodendrocyte- and astrocyte-specific deletions show no evident anomaly
Need: restore WWOX protein in neurons by gene addition
A neuronal compartment suffices in the mouse for survival and glycaemia; a neuron-directed vector does not reach the radial-glia substrate
Treatment precedes the endpoints it is judged on, so prevention and recovery cannot be told apart
C01 AAV9-WWOX: spike-wave discharges, one dose, n = 5
C04 AAV9-WWOX: survival and the other endpoint families at the high dose
Treated at P0 to P5 and judged from P10; no phenotype measured at the day of injection; later treatment not explored (authors)
Organoids: neuron-directed AAV9 at week 10 reduced hyperexcitability present at week 7 (read at week 16); radial glia not corrected
Pre-treatment baseline in the same animals or an age-matched cohort at injection day (glucose, weight, spike rate, myelin)
Treated-after-onset arms with a same-age untreated comparator; persistence beyond week 16 in organoids

edges.note: Loss in neurons alone reproduces the phenotype.
Same vector class in a human model, not the same preparation.

chains.title: Integrated stress response: sign conflict
chains.question: Is the integrated stress response raised, lowered or unchanged in WWOX-deficient neural cells? Three systems give three answers at transcript level.

nodes.label: Human WWOX-knockout organoid (4 against 2 libraries): ISR target set LOWER than chance
Neural progenitors with WWOX silenced (one library per arm): ISR target set HIGHER at both stages
Mouse P17 brain, four deletion contrasts: ISR set inside its matched null in all four; Atf4 mRNA lower (not an ISR call)
Fly neuronal knockdown with amyloid: Atf4 staining up (6 against 6), not without amyloid
Need: ISR activity, attenuate a possible over-activation; direction uncertain
UNRESOLVED: the sign differs between systems; transcripts only, no protein or phosphorylation measured
Which eIF2 kinase carries any ISR is unmeasured in every Wwox system
E01 ISR modulators (eIF2B-targeting class): outside-WWOX rows only
Adult ALS: an eIF2B activator engaged its target, no clinical benefit (ratio 1.04)
Children with vanishing white matter, single arm: hazard ratio 0.33 against registry controls; serious adverse events in about three quarters
Fly mitochondrial-synthetase seizure model: GCN2 or ATF4 knockdown lowers bang sensitivity
Isogenic null and corrected neural lines: phospho-eIF2alpha, ATF4 protein, targets, translation, kinase attribution; decision table fixed in advance
